summary: Verified the QCM/flashcard/modal overflow fix for long-option content on the 'Posture professionnelle' sheet (Domain E) across mobile (375x667) and desktop (1280x800), plus non-regression on login/logout, progress/leaderboard, and domain/unit filters. 1 backend test file + 7 browser checks, all passing (one browser check needed a stabilizing explicit-visibility wait after a flaky first run, not an app bug).

checks.criterion: QCM long options mobile: validate button reachable, all 4 options reachable, validation advances to next card
checks.name: quiz-long-options-mobile-validate
checks.evidence: Mobile 375x667: quiz-validate-button bounding box fully within viewport (y+height<=667) before and after picking quiz-option-0; study-progress advanced from CARTE 1/2 to CARTE 2/2 after validation. Screenshots: quiz-before-pick, quiz-after-validate.

checks.criterion: Same long QCM usable on mobile 375x667 AND desktop 1280x800, full 2-card flow to study-score
checks.name: quiz-long-options-desktop-full-flow
checks.evidence: Desktop 1280x800: validate button stayed within viewport across both cards of Domain E sheet; completed the full flow (card1 -> card2 -> study-score visible). Screenshots: quiz-card2, quiz-score-desktop. Mobile coverage provided by quiz-long-options-mobile-validate.

checks.criterion: Flashcard mode with long answer: known/review buttons reachable and advance the card
checks.name: flashcard-long-answer-buttons-reachable
checks.evidence: Mobile 375x667: study-reveal-button click showed study-answer-panel; study-known-button and study-review-button both had bounding boxes fully within viewport; clicking known-button advanced study-progress to CARTE 2/2. Screenshots: flashcard-long-answer, flashcard-advanced.

checks.criterion: Non-regression: upload modal and progress modal do not overflow on mobile 375x667
checks.name: modals-no-overflow-mobile
checks.evidence: Mobile 375x667: opened open-upload-modal-button dialog and open-progress-button dialog; each had at least one visible action button fully within viewport (y+height<=667). Screenshots: upload-modal, progress-modal.

checks.name: login-logout-regression
checks.evidence: Logged in with lea.martin@ifsi.fr/Promo2026! -> library visible (domain-tab-a); opened user-menu-trigger without console error beyond expected pre-login 401; logout-button returned to login-email-input screen. Screenshots: logged-in-library, user-menu-open, logged-out.

checks.criterion: Non-regression progress and leaderboard after answering cards
checks.name: progress-leaderboard-updates
checks.evidence: Recorded baseline answered count via GET /api/progress/me, answered one Domain E flashcard (known), reopened progress dialog: stat-answered increased (after > before); tab-leaderboard showed leaderboard-row-0 with 'moi' badge text present for the logged-in user. Screenshots: dialog-opened, progress-stats, leaderboard.

checks.name: test_tscheck_progress_regression
checks.evidence: POST /progress/answer -> 201 {recorded:true}; GET /progress/me answered incremented by 1 (assert stats.answered == answered_before+1); GET /progress/leaderboard includes my_id entry with is_me=True. Ran via `python -m pytest`: 1 passed.

checks.name: domain-unit-filter-session
checks.evidence: Clicked domain-tab-a then unit-tab-A1 without console error, grid filtered; start-session-button opened an aggregated session showing study-progress. Screenshots: filtered-a1, session-started.

action_items: Note: initial run of progress-leaderboard-updates hit a 30s timeout on stat-answered right after closing the study dialog with Escape (likely a timing/animation race, not reproduced after adding an explicit toBeVisible wait on open-progress-button before clicking). Classified as flaky, not a bug, since the rerun with the added wait passed cleanly and the underlying feature (answer -> progress -> leaderboard) works via both UI and backend test.
notes: 8 acceptance_matrix criteria covered by 7 browser checks + 1 backend test file (progress/leaderboard criterion has both UI and API coverage as it is API-backed and UI-facing).
Console errors observed across all checks were exclusively the expected 401 on /api/auth/me probe before login (per spec_deviations/acceptance matrix allowance) — no unexpected 4xx/5xx observed.
No application code was modified; only browser checks (/app/.emergent/scripts/checks/) and this report were added, plus reuse of the pre-existing backend test file.
